title: Effect of an input-head control action
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $c$ be a configuration on input $x$ with $k$ work tapes, let $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and let $q$ be an optional state. Applying the control action with movement $m$ and successor state $q$ leaves all work-tape contents, work-tape head positions, and output unchanged, sets the state to $q$, and moves the input head by $m$ with clamping at the boundary positions.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration on input $x$ with $k$ work tapes
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean
alphabet on input $x$, let $m \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ be a movement, and let $q$
be an optional state.  Applying the control action for $m$ and $q$ to $c$
yields the configuration that agrees with $c$ on all work-tape contents,
work-head positions, and output, whose state is $q$, and whose input head is
that of $c$ moved by $m$ with clamping at the two boundary blanks.
